goals.title: Select the relevant inventory
goals.concept: Inventory type and time context determine which infrastructure entities are comparable.
goals.narration: Select the relevant inventory and scenario interval.
goals.reasoning: The correct entity level prevents host, container, and service signals from being conflated.
goals.evidence: The inventory shows the scenario entities.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the ${var.inventory} inventory so we're comparing the same kind of entity when looking for an outlier.
demonstration.reasoning: Hosts, pods, containers, and services describe different ownership levels. Comparing like entities gives us a meaningful baseline.
demonstration.evidence: The inventory now lists comparable entities at the ${var.inventory} level. We can look for an outlier in the next view.

hints: Choose the entity level that owns the reported resource.
Select ${var.inventory}; Show me can demonstrate it.

goals.title: Isolate the decisive entity and metric
goals.concept: Grouping and peer comparison reveal outliers hidden by aggregate health.
goals.narration: Filter or group entities and select the relevant metric.
goals.reasoning: The abnormal entity must be compared with healthy peers or an earlier period.
goals.evidence: The selected metric contains the scenario signal.

demonstration.narration: I'll compare ${var.metric} across peers and over the incident period to see whether one entity stands out.
demonstration.reasoning: An overall health average can hide one saturated or imbalanced entity. A peer or period comparison shows whether the pattern is exceptional.
demonstration.evidence: The ${var.metric} chart now shows the outlier, ${truth.finding}. Treat it as a hypothesis until another event corroborates its timing.

hints: Compare the resource named in the brief across entities or time.
Use grouping, sorting, and the metric selector.
Select ${var.metric}; Show me can point to it.

goals.title: Correlate supporting evidence
goals.concept: Resource correlation is stronger when the timing aligns with a restart, log, or latency event.
goals.narration: Open supporting metric detail or correlated logs.
goals.reasoning: Correlation checks that the resource pattern aligns with observed impact.
goals.evidence: The supporting record contains the corroborating scenario fact.

demonstration.narration: I'll open the outlier's detail and related logs at the same time to see whether the resource change lines up with the reported issue.
demonstration.reasoning: A resource spike alone does not prove customer impact or causation. Matching its entity and timing to another observable signal tests the relationship.
demonstration.evidence:
The supporting record should align with the outlier’s entity and time.

That independent correlation turns the metric pattern into evidence for the conclusion: ${truth.conclusion}

hints: Check whether the timing aligns with another observable signal.
Use the entity detail or logs pivot.
Open correlated logs; Show me can demonstrate the read-only pivot.

goals.title: Submit a metric-supported conclusion
goals.concept: State the entity, pattern, and time relationship without proposing an administrative repair.
goals.narration: Record the conclusion and supporting evidence.
goals.reasoning: The scenario tests Kibana interpretation, not infrastructure operation.
goals.evidence: The response cites the metric and correlation.
hints: State the resource pattern and affected entity.
Include finding, scope, conclusion, and evidence references.
